title: Foreign defense technology sharing depends on a specialized permission system whose speed and trust vary by request
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-108435 review of Department of Defense technology release and foreign disclosure processes
geography: United States and foreign governments or international organizations requesting U.S. defense articles, services, or sensitive military technology

observations.period: 2024–2026; foreign military sales and technology-release process context

denominator.unit: more than 100 foreign governments and international organizations that request U.S. defense articles or services

annual_trfd_cases.unit: foreign military sales cases that DOD reported undergo technology-release and foreign-disclosure review each year, approximately

follow_on_or_existing_precedent.unit: percent of TRFD cases officials estimated represent continuation of existing sales and are generally approved under existing policy or precedent

discovery_duration.value: a few days to a year
discovery_duration.unit: official estimate of time from request to determining whether applicable policy or precedent exists

delay_frequency.unit: official estimate of requests delayed during the discovery phase

observations.method: GAO reviewed DOD documents and training materials, met with DOD and State officials and operational personnel, and attended a foreign-disclosure-officer course; reported volumes and timing are official estimates rather than independently validated administrative counts.
observations.uncertainty: The source does not provide a public case-level dataset, complete request denominator, partner-by-partner approval rate, delivery result, or outcome after a technology transfer.
observations.subgroup: Foreign partners and international organizations, existing-policy or precedent cases, new or sensitive technology cases, and requests involving multiple military departments or specialized interagency reviews.
observations.counterinterpretation: Long or specialized review can protect security and preserve technological advantage; most cases reportedly move through existing pathways, so the presence of a complex approval system does not by itself show dysfunction or partner distrust.

denominator.unit: TRFD reform action items in the DOD implementation plan

completed_reforms.unit: action items officials reported completed as of May 2026

planned_completion.unit: DOD officials' target to complete the current reform set

urgent_ukraine_example.value: reviews that typically took a year were completed within weeks, and some within hours, after urgent prioritization for Ukraine; officials said this relied heavily on overtime and deprioritized other work

partner_visibility.value: limited visibility into causes of delayed approvals can cause frustration for foreign partners awaiting a response

observations.method: GAO assessed the reform plan and obtained written and oral updates from DOD officials on progress as of May 2026.
observations.uncertainty: Reform completion is reported by DOD officials and does not establish that request times improved, that partners received requested technology, or that urgent prioritization produced durable alliance or industrial effects.
observations.subgroup: TRFD policy stakeholders, military departments, foreign-disclosure officers, foreign partners, and urgent versus ordinary requests.
observations.counterinterpretation: Prioritizing urgent cases can be appropriate during war or crisis; deprioritized routine work may reflect a deliberate allocation choice rather than administrative failure.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies request volume, review timing, distributed decision-making, partner-visibility, urgent prioritization, and reform-progress findings.

boundary: This record establishes a permission and administrative-timing layer between a foreign partner's request and possible defense-technology transfer. It does not establish approval or denial for a named partner, delivery, use, partner consent, deterrence, battlefield effect, export revenue, or durable trust.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO accessible HTML report retrieved and hashed; underlying classified or controlled DOD reports, case files, and partner records not retained
